subject.title: [Bug]: Deep-profile release gate treats instrumented RSS as baseline-eligible

question: Should maintainers land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102894 as the fix for this issue after exact-head release-gate proof, or keep the Kova performance gate strict for profiled resource failures?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes release automation's fail-open boundary and the issue is maintainer-owned and protected.

options.title: Review And Land The Linked PR
options.body: Use the open linked PR as the canonical fix if its current-head proof still accepts only profiled resource-only reports and rejects baseline, functional, harness, timeout, auth, and non-resource failures.

options.title: Keep The Gate Strict
options.body: Reject the tolerance and address profiler overhead in Kova thresholds, profiling policy, or release workflow expectations instead.

options.title: Ask For A Narrower Adapter
options.body: Keep this issue open and request stricter fixture or predicate coverage before allowing any DO_NOT_SHIP report to become effective success.

recommendation.title: Review And Land The Linked PR
recommendation.body: Use the open linked PR as the canonical fix if its current-head proof still accepts only profiled resource-only reports and rejects baseline, functional, harness, timeout, auth, and non-resource failures.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the linked issue and PR path and has the strongest recent history on the performance workflow and Kova helper.
